limits.sandbox: CPU-only Docker python@c61cffc3, no network, 256 MB, 1 CPU, 10 s per grade

scheduling.placement: agent j of case c on replica/grader host (c+j)%4
scheduling.concurrency_note: each arm alone on the fleet: 20 client requests per node <= 25

serving.launch: inkling/serve.sh with MEM=0.75 (cookbook dgx-spark/nvfp4/dspark + text-only, ctx 131072; KV pool ~1.08M tokens per node since 2026-11-21 16:25 Europe/Warsaw)
serving.adapter: inkling/shim.py (vLLM dialect; client disconnects are shim:client_cancels)

frozen_note: Frozen 2026-11-21 before any call with seeds 4-6 on coding-hard-v1. Fresh seeds on the existing 24 evaluation tasks (owner: "on the existing one with a fresh seed"); agent seed offset 1700 is new, so every agent sample is new. An offline replay of the seed 1-3 run (inkling/sim_coding_early_stop.py, results/swarm-cancel-hard6-v1/REPORT.md) predicted: stopping at the first feedback-passing candidate in time keeps 69/72 (the slot-order rule) for about 35-45 % fewer agent tokens and 55-61 % less case wall; contracts added nothing under early stop, so this live test uses public feedback only.
selection: the first proposal in TIME order that passes ALL feedback cases ends the case: other agents of the case are terminated, queued ones never start; solved if it passes ALL holdout cases
question: Does stopping a coding case at the first proposal that passes the public tests (E) keep the accuracy of running all 8 agents to the end (F) while cutting server tokens and wall time?
execution: Each arm alone on the fleet via inkling/coding_arms.py (fresh admission with the shim sha below, prefix-cache flush, server counters before and after, idle wait, GPU energy). Arms run one after another, E first.

primary_outcomes.tokens: Server-counted generated tokens per case (delta of sglang:generation_tokens_total on the four nodes / 72), E vs F.
primary_outcomes.wall: Arm wall time and per-case stop time, E vs F.
primary_outcomes.selection_effect: Noise-free selection effect inside F: holdout result of the first feedback-passing proposal in TIME order vs in SLOT order, same proposals (difference in solved cases).
primary_outcomes.accuracy: Solved/72 E vs F, paired two-sided exact sign test over (task, seed) (contains run-to-run generation noise, about +-4 cases).

decision_rule: Early stop becomes the default for the Inkling coding swarm if: the noise-free selection effect inside F is >= -1 case AND E server tokens per case <= 0.80 x F AND E arm wall < F. E vs F solved is reported with its sign test, not used as a gate (run-to-run noise).
secondary_outcomes: GPU energy per solved case; cancelled and never-started agents; per-case stop time distribution; One Inkling (agent 0 of F); oracle (any feedback-and-holdout pass) in F.
exclusions: None; all 72 cases of each arm count.
resume_rule: As in earlier coding plans: on an operational fault the runner stops admissions; the same arm is continued only for unfinished cases with the same seeds and documented as an amendment.
smoke: Throwaway smoke (not part of the study) on development task dev-repeating_expansion, seed 9, 4 agents, early stop: agent 1 passed the public tests at 167 s, agents 0/2/3 were terminated (shim client_cancels 3, 0 upstream errors), no grading containers left on the nodes.
baseline_note: Arithmetic default is now B+ (swarm-escalate-hard7-v1); this study is about the coding swarm only.
